overview: This House resolution, known as a 'rule,' sets the terms for House debate on H.R. 1, the large budget reconciliation bill. Reconciliation is a special budget process, set up under a budget resolution (here H. Con. Res. 14), that allows tax and spending legislation to move faster and, in the Senate, avoid a filibuster. The rule automatically swaps in a revised version of the bill prepared by the Rules Committee with further changes, allows two hours of debate split among the leaders of the Budget and Ways and Means committees, permits no other amendments beyond one motion to recommit, and waives procedural objections, including a House rule that requires a three-fifths vote to pass income tax rate increases. The House adopted it on May 22, 2025.
for: Supporters say the rule allows the House to move quickly to a vote on a major budget package that had already been worked out in committee.
against: Critics say limiting debate on a bill of this size to two hours and blocking amendments from members leaves little room to examine or change its many provisions.
